sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. By filing the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

The petitioner has prayed for the following relief:
"(A) Be pleased to issue an appropriate writ, order or directions, by quashing and setting aside the impugned judgment and order dated 19.11.2025 passed by the 6th Additional Session Judge, Banaskantha at Deesa below Exh.18 in Criminal Revision Application No. 104/2025 (Annexure D) as well as order dated 04.08.2025 passed by the 6th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Palanpur in Criminal Case No.4791/2013 (Annexure B) and further be pleased to allow the application made by the applicant under section 93 of the CRPC.

(C) Pass such other and further order(s) as the Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the interest of justice."
2. The facts and circumstances giving rise to the filing of the present petition are such that the petitioner herein had lodged a complaint before the Court of Competent Jurisdiction alleging offence punishable under Section 406, 420, 120(B), 504, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

The learned Competent Court had ordered an inquiry under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and thus, an offence being MCase No.01/2011 was registered against the accused at Palanpur Taluka Police Station.
The investigating agency after conclusion of investigation filed charge-sheet against the accused persons.
It is the case of the petitioner and prosecution against the accused that an Agreement to Sale had been forged in the name of the present petitioner.
While filing the charge-sheet, the investigation officer had declared before the Court that the questioned Agreement to Sale could not be traced despite all efforts being made to find out the same.

After examination of few witnesses during the course of trial, the petitioner herein had submitted an application seeking issuance of search warrant under Section 93 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the Agreement to Sale in question.

The said application was dismissed by the 6th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Palanpur vide order dated 04.08.2025 interalia on the ground that the authority, against whom the warrant was sought, was NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/17413/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/01/2026 undefined not clarified.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order the petitioner had preferred Criminal Revision Application No.105 of the 2025 before the learned Sessions Court at Deesa.

entities.text: Criminal Revision Application No.105 of the 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The said revision application was also dismissed by the learned Sessions Court vide ordered at 19.11.2025 interalia holding that asking the accused to produce such document would amount to asking the accused to be a witness against his ownself.
Being agreed by these orders the petitioner has come before this Court by filing the present petition.
3. Heard learned advocate Shri. Vishal B. Mehta appearing for the petitioner.
He submitted that the investigating agency had though made attempts to find out the document in question, the said document is still not found out.
In the absence of the original document it would be difficult for prosecution to prove the charges levelled against the accused.
He further submitted that both the courts below have committed a grave error in dismissing the application filed by the petitioner.

What was prayed by the petitioner before the Trial Court was a direction to the police authorities to produce the document in question by recovering it from the police to the person who may be in possession of that document.
The petitioner had not sought any direction to the accused asking them to produce the document in question.
Therefore, there was no question of the accused being compelled to be a witness against his own self as observed by the learned Sessions Court.

He therefore submitted to allow the present petition and quash and set aside the orders impugned in the present petition and direct the investigating agency to recover the document in question and produce it NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/17413/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/01/2026 undefined before the concerned Trial Court.
4. Learned APP has opposed the present petition interalia contending that all efforts were made by the investigation officer during the course of investigation to recover the document in question.

sentences.text: However, it could not be recovered despite all efforts being made by the investigation officer to recover the same.
Therefore, there is no requirement for issuing any direction to the police authorities as prayed for.
He therefore submitted to dismiss the present application.
5. Heard learned advocates for the parties.
It is the case of the petitioner that an Agreement to Sale came to be forged by the accused and on the basis of the said forged document, the parcel of land in question was sought to be transacted.
The material available on record suggests that the investigation officer had made all attempts to recover the document in question during the course of investigation.
However, the said document was not found out.
The charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer against the accused also reflects these facts.
The perusal of the applications filed by the petitioner before the courts below also indicate that the petitioner is also not sure as regards the whereabouts of the document in question.
The learned Trial Court appears to be right in observing that it is not stated in the application as to who is in possession of the said document.
It is also not clear as to against whom the warrant under Section 93 of the CRPC is required to be issued.
The prayer made by the petitioner before the learned Trial Court is as vague as it could be as it does not indicate anything with regard to the whereabouts of the document in question.

Moreover, when the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/17413/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/01/2026 undefined investigating agency, during the course of investigation, has made all attempts to recover the document in question and has not found out the document, there is no question of issuance of any further direction to the investigating agency to find out such document.
6. In that view of the matter, both the courts below cannot be said to have committed any error in passing the orders impugned in the present petition.
Hence the petition stands dismissed.
